title: for Loops and Counter-Controlled Iteration
learningObjectives: Explain for loops and counter-controlled iteration and their execution flow.
Trace condition checks and state changes across iterations.
Select a suitable loop structure for a given problem.
Identify common termination and boundary mistakes.
Apply the loop pattern in an original small program.

understand.concept: A for header combines initialization, condition, and update. Initialization runs once; update runs after the body.
understand.whyItMatters: For loops make counter-controlled repetition and boundaries easy to see.
understand.explain: Read the header as setup → test → body → update. Verify how many values pass the condition.

examples.title: Print even values
examples.explanation: Custom update step produces even numbers.

examples.title: Reverse countdown
examples.explanation: The condition and decrement move toward termination.

examples.title: Three attempts
examples.explanation: The header clearly expresses three iterations.

practise.guidedTask: Trace and annotate each of the five for Loops and Counter-Controlled Iteration examples. For every iteration, record the relevant variable values, condition result and action. Change one input or bound and predict the new behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program demonstrating for loops and counter-controlled iteration in a practical scenario. Include at least three typical tests, two boundary tests, and one invalid or termination test. Explain how the loop terminates.
hints: Keep initialization, test and update aligned.
Check how many values the condition admits.
Choose an increment that reaches termination.

questions.prompt: What runs once before the first for test?

questions.explanation: Update follows the body and precedes next condition.
